assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles, followed by the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum materials as a tunable platform for correlation physics. It is original, conceptually clear and has spawned a large field across graphene, TMD moire systems and beyond. As a theorist of electronic structure I value that a relatively simple band-structure idea predicted a regime where interactions dominate.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit is naturally Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011), with the experimental breakthrough led by Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (2018). The three-person configuration pairs prediction with discovery cleanly. Subsequent contributors in the supplied credit set are not included, and the role of earlier twisted-bilayer band-structure work (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto) is something I recall but cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Correlated insulators and superconductivity have been reproduced by many independent groups and the platform is now broad, so the discovery is robust. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated, but the existence and importance of the phenomena are not. Timing is reasonable, roughly eight years after the experiments.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is unsettled, which could make the interpretation of the superconductivity less stable than the flat-band and insulator findings.
Fair weight to earlier theoretical work on twisted-bilayer electronic structure is uncertain from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions turned spin-dependent tunnelling into a practical effect and underlies read heads and magnetic random-access memory. The physics of spin-polarised tunnelling and, later, coherent tunnelling through crystalline MgO barriers is of clear lasting importance and is close to my own field of magnetism and spin-dependent electronic structure.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 room-temperature results by Moodera and by Miyazaki are decisive; Parkin's contributions to optimised junctions and MgO-based devices were important. The assignment is plausible but sensitive: Julliere's earlier low-temperature work, the first-principles prediction of large MgO-based TMR by Butler and by Mathon, and the Yuasa and Parkin MgO experiments are not all representable in the supplied credit set. Parkin's separate GMR-related work also complicates how a prize would be framed given the 2007 award.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been confirmed in many laboratories and is industrially deployed for decades. Recognition is not premature; if anything it is late, and the main issue is a fair and clean configuration.
uncertainties: Whether the best prize configuration should include the MgO coherent-tunnelling theory and experiments, which are outside the supplied three names.
Overlap in subject matter with the 2007 GMR prize may lead others to see it as a continuation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, established an entire class of materials with protected boundary states. It built on band theory and spin-orbit coupling and transformed how band structures are classified and searched for in materials databases. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the central theoretical contributions (2005). Molenkamp's group provided the decisive early experimental demonstration in HgTe (2007), following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the supplied credit set; this is a real attribution concern. The three-person configuration is defensible but incomplete in credit history.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by transport and ARPES across multiple material families, and the concept is stable. The 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions and TKNN-type physics, so this is a distinct but related follow-up and well matured.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and of the experimental three-dimensional TI work (e.g. Hasan, Kane-Moore-Balents-Fu related) from the supplied names.
Possible perception of closeness to the 2016 topological prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, exact in infinite dimensions, and with LDA+DMFT it became a workhorse for real correlated materials such as transition-metal oxides and f-electron systems. It explains the Mott transition, coexistence of quasiparticles and Hubbard bands and spectral properties. From my own work with electronic-structure methods, I regard its impact on quantitative materials theory as very high, though it is a method rather than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt (1989) introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, and Georges and Kotliar (1992) mapped it onto an impurity problem; this is how I recall the history, not independently verified here. Metzner and Muller-Hartmann are not in the supplied credit set, leaving credit incomplete. Within the supplied names, Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt is a reasonable trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with more than three decades of use and validation against spectroscopy; limitations of local self-energy and cluster extensions are known but well studied. Recognition would be timely, if anything overdue.
uncertainties: Methodological contribution rather than an experimental discovery; the committee may differ on whether this fits the prize criteria.
Credit allocation between the 1989 limit and the 1992 impurity mapping is contested in places.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of magnetic skyrmion lattices in chiral magnets and of their emergent electrodynamics created a new area of topological magnetism with real-space textures, ultra-low current-density manipulation and a link to spintronic memory concepts. The conceptual clarity of an emergent gauge field acting on conduction electrons is attractive, and the field is closely connected to magnetism and spin dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's neutron-scattering observation in MnSi (2009) and Tokura's real-space imaging in FeGe and related materials are key experimental steps; Rosch contributed the theory of skyrmion dynamics and emergent electrodynamics. The original theoretical prediction by Bogdanov and colleagues, and the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya basis, are historically important and not in the supplied names, which raises a credit concern.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed in many materials including room-temperature interfaces, but the technological promise (racetrack-type devices) is not yet realised, and the pinning and stability issues remain. The science is mature enough; the application impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Bogdanov's earlier prediction is outside the supplied credit set.
Unrealised device applications may weaken the claim for broad lasting impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised clean, tunable Hubbard-model physics, including the superfluid-to-Mott transition and later quantum gas microscopy, giving a controlled quantum simulator of many-body models that are hard to solve classically. It is a conceptual and experimental landmark connecting AMO physics to condensed-matter theory.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch provided the key theoretical proposal for Bose-Hubbard physics in lattices, Greiner and Bloch the experimental demonstration of the Mott transition and subsequent microscopy. Dalibard, Cirac and others are also credited elsewhere in the list, and the 5-name credit set exceeds three, so any three-person selection leaves out major figures, including Hansch-related contributions to lattice cooling that I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed and reproduced worldwide for two decades. The 2001 prize recognised Bose-Einstein condensation, so this is a distinct follow-on; programmable simulation is still progressing, so the fully realised promise is not yet complete.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among at least five major contributors is difficult.
Overlap with other atomic-physics and quantum-information candidates on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-resolution ARPES turned photoemission into a quantitative probe of momentum-resolved electronic structure in correlated materials, enabling direct measurement of Fermi surfaces, gaps, kinks and pseudogaps in cuprates. This speaks directly to the need to compare calculated and measured spectra, and has been central to testing electronic-structure theory in quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen both made early decisive cuprate ARPES contributions; as I recall, other instrument and technique developers (e.g. Hufner, Dessau, Hasan, Damascelli and others) also contributed. The two-person configuration is clean but may understate a broad community effort and the instrumental development behind it.
assessment.maturity: The technique is extensively validated and widely used, and the basic measurements are reproducible. However, interpretation of cuprate spectra such as the pseudogap remains debated, which limits the claim to a definitive discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the prize rationale centres on technique development or on specific physical discoveries is unclear.
Many contributors are outside the supplied credit set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third collinear magnetic class with spin-split bands and zero net magnetisation, predicted from symmetry and first-principles calculations. It is original, directly relevant to magnetism, and promising for spintronics. I find the symmetry-based classification and the DFT-driven material predictions appealing.
assessment.attribution: Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth and collaborators articulated the symmetry classification and the name; the earlier predictions of related spin-split physics by others (e.g. Hayami, Yanagi and Kusunose, Yuan and Zunger) complicate priority. The supplied three-name configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation by ARPES and related probes in MnTe and CrSb appeared only in recent years, and device-relevant consequences are limited so far. This is likely premature for a prize in 2026, but it is a strong candidate for later years.
uncertainties: Independent experimental confirmation is recent and the breadth of materials still developing.
Priority questions concerning earlier related theoretical work are unresolved.
